rules.rule: Fæder is masculine; selected endingless genitive/dative singular fæder, with fæderes/fædere accepted; plural follows fæderas/fædera/fæderum/fæderas. Cook43.8 gives an exception to the strong masculine system, not an instruction to derive an umlaut dat singular.

Gāt: N/A singular gāt, selected G singular gāte (variant gǣt), D singular gǣt (variant gāte); N/A plural gǣt, G plural gāta, D plural gātum. The long vowel alternation is ā/ǣ; no -as plural or fictitious gǣtum.

Hand/woruld use strong feminine morphology with endingless accusative singular. Cook p297 explicitly directs hand to51.1.3; this lexical cross-reference licenses51.1 even though hand is absent from its exemplar list. Selected genitive/dative hande/worulde; source-authorized -a variants are accepted. A syncretic adjective ending alone does not disambiguate hand phrases.

Selected dryhten/dēofol/ęngel retain full nominative/accusative singular but use dryhtn-/dēofl-/ęngl- with endings; stem diagnostics control every cell. Compounds giesthūs and cweartern retain their terminal noun stems.

Apply complete prior strong/weak adjective systems. Retained-vowel disyllables, -e adjectives, long-stem unrihtwīs and double-consonant synfull have explicit diagnostics; swīðra has weak comparative morphology only. Displayed instrumental forms remain recognition unless the coordinator names an explicit productive means frame.

Hungry, sick, naked and unrighteous adjectives can name persons in the weak declension; the new people senses are separately assigned. Their case is governed by the containing clause, not by English the.
